description.narrative: The development objective of the Northern Uplands Health Support Project in Vietnam is to increase utilization of district health services especially among Decision 139 beneficiaries in the Northern Upland Provinces through: (i) strengthening of district hospitals, and (ii) reducing financial constraints to accessing health services. The first project component will strengtheni district-level health services. This component aims to improve the quality of district hospitals by; (i) strengthening the health workforce capacity and developing pilot models to increase staff retention in Northern Upland (NU) provinces; (ii) provide basic medical equipment and selective facility repair and refurbishment; and (iii) improve hospital management. The second project component will increase financial access to healthcare services for decision 139 beneficiaries. This component aims to address demand-side constraints of access to health services by piloting mechanisms to further reduce financial barriers for the Decision 139 beneficiaries in the project provinces. The project will support provincial and district agencies in strengthening monitoring, reporting and supervision of the Health Care Fund for the Poor (HCFP) implementation at all levels. The third project component is monitoring, evaluation, and project management. This component will support the set up and management of the Central Project Management Unit (CPMU) and Provincial Project Management Units (PPMUs) through: (i) consulting services to cover technical issues as well as procurement, financial management, and disbursement; (ii) training of project management staff; (iii) provision of necessary office equipment; (iv) financing of incremental operating costs, and (v) monitoring and evaluation activities, including the baseline data collection, indicator updates, mid-term reviews, end of project completion report and audits.

The project development objective is: Increase utilization of district health services especially among Decision 139 beneficiaries in the Northern Upland Provinces through (i) strengthening of district hospitals and (ii) reducing financial constraints to accessing health services.
